AgentSessionOut.description:
A coding-agent session that touched this entity, or something beneath it.

Ordered by when we first saw it, so at run level the first entry is the
session the run originated in — the same one recorded in
`runs.foreign_keys.<agent>_session_id`.

`captured` is deliberately NOT here. Whether a transcript exists is the
engine's answer, not this database's: capture is a per-device permission a
user can switch off, so a recorded session with no transcript is an
expected state. The page resolves it against the transcripts corpus at
render time and shows captured / pending / not-captured there. Asserting it
here would mean this endpoint lying whenever the engine disagreed.
AgentSessionOut.title: AgentSessionOut

AgentSessionsOut.description: A bounded page of sessions plus the honest total.
AgentSessionsOut.title: AgentSessionsOut

AnchorLevel.description:
The three vertically-movable artifact anchors (workspace/shared-folder files
move via the share/unshare rails, not here). Ordered run < experiment < project
so `move` can tell a promote (derive the target up the chain) from a demote
(target_id required, and validated to sit inside the current subtree).
AnchorLevel.title: AnchorLevel

AnchorType.description:
What a summary (and a summary_refresh queue row) is about.

Mirrors the `summary_refresh.anchor_type` CHECK constraint -- adding a member
here without widening that CHECK makes every enqueue for it fail (silently,
since `enqueue_summary_refresh` swallows to protect the domain write).
AnchorType.title: AnchorType

ArtifactMove.description:
Move an artifact vertically along its own run->experiment->project chain.

`target_id` is derived server-side for a promote (a run has exactly one
experiment, an experiment one project) and REQUIRED for a demote (a parent has
many children); a demote target is validated to sit inside the artifact's current
subtree, so this can never express a lateral move to a sibling.
ArtifactMove.title: ArtifactMove

ArtifactPinImpact.description:
What a delete would break (D7): the actual projects and experiments whose
manifests or lineage edges pin one of this artifact's versions.
ArtifactPinImpact.title: ArtifactPinImpact

ArtifactScope.description:
Which anchor levels a run's artifact listing spans.

OWN (default) is the run's own artifacts only -- the historical behavior, so the
run bundle, dashboard, and `artifact_count` are untouched. INHERITED and ALL are
opt-in reads for the live-run/CLI case where a run needs to see what has been
promoted to its experiment/project. Inheritance is resolution/listing on THIS
endpoint only; it never widens the run's own count surfaces.
ArtifactScope.title: ArtifactScope

ArtifactVersionCreate.description:
Append a version. Either PROMOTE from an existing artifact (`from_artifact_id`,
zero-copy: the version pins that artifact's content_hash + full r2:// uri + size)
OR supply the pointer identity directly.
ArtifactVersionCreate.title: ArtifactVersionCreate

BinaryNode.description:
Two operands, applied pointwise. `mod` is math.fmod (sign follows the
dividend), `pow` returns NaN where the result would be complex.
BinaryNode.title: BinaryNode

ClampNode.description:
Bound a curve to [lo, hi]. Expressible as min(max(x, lo), hi), but that
reads as arithmetic; this reads as intent, and is one node instead of four
against the node cap.
ClampNode.title: ClampNode

ClientCapabilitiesIn.description: The complete allowlisted local snapshot. Raw configuration is forbidden.
ClientCapabilitiesIn.title: ClientCapabilitiesIn

ClientKind.description: First-party clients that may report their installed version.
ClientKind.title: ClientKind

ClientRegistrationIn.description:
RFC 7591 dynamic client registration request. We accept the standard
metadata but fix grant/response types and the (none) auth method ourselves.
ClientRegistrationIn.title: ClientRegistrationIn

ClientStatusOut.description: Server-side update-banner decision for the authenticated user.
ClientStatusOut.title: ClientStatusOut

ClientUpdateStatus.description: How urgently one observed client should be updated.
ClientUpdateStatus.title: ClientUpdateStatus

CmpNode.description:
A comparison as a 0/1 mask, so it composes with ordinary arithmetic:
multiply by it to gate a term, or feed it to `cond` as a branch test.
NaN on either side yields NaN, never a silent False.
CmpNode.title: CmpNode

CoalesceNode.description:
Replace a non-finite result with a fallback. The ONLY node that does not
propagate NaN — everything else does, so without this a single divide-by-zero
silently removes that step from the curve rather than showing a chosen value.
CoalesceNode.title: CoalesceNode

CondNode.description:
Piecewise selection: `when` non-zero picks `then`, zero picks
`otherwise`. The guard for divide-by-zero — `cond(b != 0, a / b, 0)` keeps
the step instead of dropping it as non-finite.
CondNode.title: CondNode

CoordinateOut.description:
One catalog row of the run's coordinate space (0060): a non-empty coordinate
plus which fact tables have landed on it — coordinate enumeration without a
fact-table scan.
CoordinateOut.title: CoordinateOut

CreatorKind.description:
The credential kind that wrote a row. See the module docstring: this is the
credential, not a proven actor type.
CreatorKind.title: CreatorKind

DerivedProvenance.description:
Client-supplied provenance for a DERIVED batch (0087): what computed these
points after the fact (an agent backfilling AUROC onto a completed run). The
server stamps `computed_at` and `created_by` on top — clients cannot forge
either. Folded keep-first into the series catalog, like `agg`.
DerivedProvenance.title: DerivedProvenance

DeviceAuthorizationStart.description:
Start a first-party CLI browser handoff.

PKCE is mandatory even though the high-entropy device code is already a
bearer secret: it binds the exchange to the CLI process that initiated it
if a terminal transcript or launch URL is copied elsewhere.
DeviceAuthorizationStart.title: DeviceAuthorizationStart

DeviceGrantOut.description: One credential minted by an approval. `token` is plaintext, delivered ONCE.
DeviceGrantOut.title: DeviceGrantOut

DeviceTokenCreated.description:
Exchange result.

The inherited top-level fields carry the `api` PAT exactly as they always
have. That shape is FROZEN: older CLIs send no `grants`, get `{api}`, and
must see a byte-identical response.

`grants` carries every credential the approval minted, including the api PAT
again, so a client that asked for a set does not have to special-case which
one landed on top.
DeviceTokenCreated.title: DeviceTokenCreated

ExperimentDetailOut.description:
The single-experiment read. Carries the sessions that touched it.

A separate model from ExperimentOut so the LIST endpoints cannot grow this field
by accident: sessions are one indexed lookup per entity, which is fine once
per page and wrong once per row.
ExperimentDetailOut.title: ExperimentDetailOut

ExperimentMetadataValuePut.description:
Replacement value for one server-allowlisted experiment metadata key.

The key is carried in the URL so the database can update it atomically
without replacing sibling metadata written by another subsystem.
ExperimentMetadataValuePut.title: ExperimentMetadataValuePut

ExperimentPatch.description:
Field-replace PATCH (D9). Only provided fields change; None = untouched.
`hypothesis`/`name` carry min_length=1 so a PATCH can never re-blank them.

NO `summary` field, deliberately. An experiment summary is GENERATED -- it
comes from the summary pipeline and lands in `metadata.summary`; there is no
client-writable door to it. The field used to exist (documented as "the home
for eval/benchmark aggregates"), but nothing in the CLI, SDK or ingest path
ever wrote one, so all it did was let a client overwrite a generated
document. Per-experiment aggregates belong on the runs that produced them.
ExperimentPatch.title: ExperimentPatch

ExperimentVersionMint.description:
Mint an immutable reproduction manifest (fold #6). `as_of` defaults to the
mint-time watermark; `exclude_run_ids` are recorded and left out of the refs.
ExperimentVersionMint.title: ExperimentVersionMint

GitHubInstallationClaim.description:
Post-install redirect claim: GitHub sends
?installation_id=...&state=...&code=... back to the Integrations page (Setup
URL), which POSTs all three here.

`state` is the signed token the install_url carried (team identity).
`code` is the user-authorization code GitHub adds when the App has
"Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation" enabled --
exchanged server-side to prove the claiming user ADMINISTERS the
installation (review F1: state alone cannot; installation ids are small
integers and the App-JWT lookup proves existence, never ownership).
Absent state is a POLICY rejection (422) except for the same-team
revival/re-claim path; absent code is a 422 when the server has the App's
OAuth client creds configured.
GitHubInstallationClaim.title: GitHubInstallationClaim

GitHubIntegrationState.description: Server-side integration state the Integrations page renders.
GitHubIntegrationState.title: GitHubIntegrationState

Grant.description:
What ONE browser approval authorizes.

A grant is a CAPABILITY, not a scope. `probe setup` asks for a set of them so
the human approves once and the consent screen shows every capability
together, instead of three separate round-trips each showing a fragment.

The distinction matters most for CAPTURE. Scopes describe what an API caller
may do to research data; they cannot express "stream this machine's prompts,
file contents and tool output off the device". Rendering that as `read` on a
consent screen would actively misdescribe it, so it gets its own name.
Grant.title: Grant

GroupedPoint.description:
One aggregated cell of a grouped read: a step bucket x one combination of the
`by` axes' values. `group` maps each requested axis to its value TYPED — the
int 0 arrives as `0`, the string "train" as `"train"` — because the coordinate
contract distinguishes them and JSON already encodes that distinction. None per
axis when a point misses it (sparse coords collapse into one NULL bucket per
axis by design), and None entirely when no axis was requested (a full
reduction). `n` is the count of finite raw points folded into this cell,
so a sparse or partially-logged coordinate is observable rather than silently
averaged over.

These were JSON TEXT until the labels reached a chart legend rendering
`"train"` with the quotes in it. Anything formatting a label must coerce at
the render boundary now, not assume `str`.
GroupedPoint.title: GroupedPoint

GroupedSeriesResult.description:
Server-side reduce/group over a run's stepped points (item 7). The aggregation
is EXPLICIT — the caller names the fn; the server never guesses a reduction
(declared per-key reduce fns arrive with the opt-in declaration layer). `by`
echoes the requested axes in order; `where` echoes the canonical coord filter.
Bounded to `max_rows` cells; page the remainder by passing `next_step` back as
`step_from`. Group labels are each axis value TYPED, so the int 1 and the
string "1" (distinct coordinates) stay distinct as JSON `1` and `"1"` without
the label itself carrying quote characters.
GroupedSeriesResult.title: GroupedSeriesResult

IndexCorpus.description:
The /v1/search corpus filter vocabulary (github.* and claude_code
transcript docs are engine-native, not custom-ingest projections).
IndexCorpus.title: IndexCorpus

LatestScalarOut.description: One series' scalar summary: its endpoint value + extent, no point scan.
LatestScalarOut.title: LatestScalarOut

LatestScalarsRequest.description:
Cross-run scalar SUMMARY read — the foundation for run-table sort/filter by a
final metric value (the MLflow `latest_metrics` / wandb Summary analog). Reads the
derived `metric_series` catalog (which already holds last/min/max per series), so
it never scans raw points.
LatestScalarsRequest.title: LatestScalarsRequest

LineageEntityType.description: The endpoints a lineage edge can connect (closed set).
LineageEntityType.title: LineageEntityType

MetricExportResult.description:
Lossless, paginated raw-point export (item 5): every point exactly once, NO
downsampling for a stable committed dataset — the faithful-export counterpart to
/series/query. Cursor on the stable metric_points id; pass `next_after_id` back as
`after_id` for the next page (null means the last currently visible page).
MetricExportResult.title: MetricExportResult

MetricSeriesOut.description: One catalog row: what/how-much/what-shape, no point scan (D15).
MetricSeriesOut.title: MetricSeriesOut

MetricSeriesSelector.description:
An exact metric-series identity used as a chart's value-typed x-axis.

Unlike a y-axis ``SeriesSelector``, dimensions are never ``None`` here: a
metric x-axis must name one concrete series or two ranks could be paired
into the same line silently.
MetricSeriesSelector.title: MetricSeriesSelector

MetricViewData.description:
An evaluated view: one stepped series. Points reuse the /series/query
shape (SeriesPoint) so chart clients need no second decoder.
MetricViewData.title: MetricViewData

MetricViewPreviewRequest.description: Un-persisted evaluation — powers the create/edit dialog's live preview.
MetricViewPreviewRequest.title: MetricViewPreviewRequest

OwnershipTransfer.description: Owner-selected existing member who will become the new owner.
OwnershipTransfer.title: OwnershipTransfer

PendingInviteOut.description: An invite shown to the invitee on /onboarding (joined to team name).
PendingInviteOut.title: PendingInviteOut

ProjectArtifactCreate.description: Project-anchored artifact (fold #22); same shape as the experiment-anchored one.
ProjectArtifactCreate.title: ProjectArtifactCreate

ProjectDetailOut.description:
The single-project read. Carries the sessions that touched it.

A separate model from ProjectOut so the LIST endpoints cannot grow this field
by accident: sessions are one indexed lookup per entity, which is fine once
per page and wrong once per row.
ProjectDetailOut.title: ProjectDetailOut

ProjectPatch.description:
Field-replace PATCH (D9). Only provided fields change; None = untouched.

`workspace_id` re-files the project into another workspace (D6: projects
stay re-fileable); it is resolved in-tenant before use (amendment #3).
ProjectPatch.title: ProjectPatch

PublicAccessOut.description:
A resource's publication state, as the team-facing surface sees it. There
is no token: the shareable link is the resource's ordinary dashboard URL.
PublicAccessOut.title: PublicAccessOut

PublicMetricSeriesOut.description:
Catalog row for the public surface: `origin` stays (the "derived" chip
is honest labeling), `provenance` is filtered to producer + computed_at.
PublicMetricSeriesOut.title: PublicMetricSeriesOut

PublicMetricViewOut.description: MetricViewOut minus `created_by` — user ids never leave the tenant.
PublicMetricViewOut.title: PublicMetricViewOut

PublicPageInfo.description:
The unfurl/page-shell read: what kind of thing this URL opens and the
resource's display identity — nothing else.
PublicPageInfo.title: PublicPageInfo

PublicRunBundle.description:
The run-page bundle minus `sessions` (coding-agent session ids) and with
lineage refs filtered by the caller to in-grant runs before validation.
PublicRunBundle.title: PublicRunBundle

PublishRequest.description: Publish (or re-publish with new settings) a resource at its own URL.
PublishRequest.title: PublishRequest

ReduceNode.description:
Collapse the whole curve to one number, broadcast back over every step.

This is what makes normalization expressible: a z-score is
`(x - reduce(mean, x)) / reduce(std, x)`, and min-max is
`(x - reduce(min, x)) / (reduce(max, x) - reduce(min, x))`.

Non-finite values are excluded from the statistic — a summary that one
divide-by-zero turns into NaN would take the entire output curve with it.
A curve with nothing finite in it reduces to NaN.

SCOPE: the statistic is taken over the ALIGNED grid, which is the inner join
across every leaf in the expression — not over the operand's whole stored
curve. `zscore(a)` alone standardizes over all of `a`; the same expression
with a sparse `b` in it standardizes over the steps `a` and `b` share. That
follows from evaluating one expression on one grid, and it is the honest
reading (the output only exists where the join does), but it is worth
knowing before comparing a normalized curve against a differently-scoped
one. The same applies to `scan` and `window`.
ReduceNode.title: ReduceNode

ResourceKind.description: Values match the dashboard's SharedResourceKind byte-for-byte.
ResourceKind.title: ResourceKind

RunBundle.description:
One request: run + coding sessions + catalog + artifact index (bounded) +
spans overview + lineage refs. Raw points are excluded (fetch via
/series/query).
RunBundle.title: RunBundle

RunCounts.description: Child-row tallies nested under RunOut.counts (dashboard contract).
RunCounts.title: RunCounts

RunDetailOut.description:
The /v1 read view of a run: RunOut plus the fold fields that are DELIBERATELY
absent from RunOut so the frozen ingest response stays byte-identical (the ingest
route keeps response_model=RunOut, which filters these out). short_id (fold #21)
is the human-facing petname the dashboard displays; created_by (fold #1), env_ref
(fold #7), foreign_keys (fold #8), and activity-aware updated_at (0071)
surface here for reads. project_id (0054) is likewise detail-only: the
run's owning project, always set.
RunDetailOut.title: RunDetailOut

RunGroupPatch.description: Field-replace PATCH (D9). Only provided fields change; None = untouched.
RunGroupPatch.title: RunGroupPatch

RunLineage.description: Ancestors + descendants of a run (recursive-CTE result).
RunLineage.title: RunLineage

SandboxDiffCounts.description:
Change tallies over the WHOLE scan (both manifests fully consumed), so a
truncated page still reports honest totals.
SandboxDiffCounts.title: SandboxDiffCounts

SandboxDiffEntry.description: One changed (or, when include_unchanged, unchanged) path in the diff.
SandboxDiffEntry.title: SandboxDiffEntry

SandboxDiffResult.description:
A trial's begin/end filesystem diff: changed-set entries + full-scan counts
+ the meta.json integrity/limits echo. `include_unchanged=false` (default)
keeps the common case tiny (D2); the rare full tree pages by `next_cursor`.
SandboxDiffResult.title: SandboxDiffResult

SandboxFileContent.description:
One added/modified file's END-state content from `end-delta.tar.gz`
(phase 2). The delta carries only end bytes — never the begin side — so this
is honestly the POST-change content, not a before/after diff (D3). A symlink
member returns its `symlink_target` and no `text`; a non-UTF-8 file returns
`is_binary=true` with no `text`; a file over the byte cap returns its head
with `truncated=true`.
SandboxFileContent.title: SandboxFileContent

SandboxFileSide.description: One file's metadata on one side of the capture window (begin or end).
SandboxFileSide.title: SandboxFileSide

ScanNode.description:
A running value over the step axis — the first operators that are NOT
pointwise. `cummax` is "best so far", the most-asked-for derived curve;
`delta` is step-over-step change.

Non-finite inputs are excluded and the scan continues, matching `_sma` in
the telemetry store: one divide-by-zero mid-curve must not destroy every
step after it. `delta` is the exception — it is a difference, not an
accumulation, so a missing endpoint yields NaN for that step alone.
ScanNode.title: ScanNode

Scope.description:
Coarse v1 authorization scopes (D2). Narrowable later; checked as explicit
sets per route, NOT as a hierarchy (a `write` token does not imply `read`).
Scope.title: Scope

ScopedUploadRequest.description:
Upload fields shared by project and experiment anchors.

The anchor comes exclusively from the URL and the R2 pointer/key are always
server-built. Forbid extras so a client-supplied ``uri`` or ``key`` is rejected
instead of being silently ignored by Pydantic.
ScopedUploadRequest.title: ScopedUploadRequest

SearchEntityType.description: Entities the exact SQL channel searches (names + slugs).
SearchEntityType.title: SearchEntityType

SemanticChunk.description:
One MATCHED chunk of a document, full content.

Not truncated to a fixed cap: when the response must shrink, the budget
drops whole chunks from the tail rather than clipping every chunk into
uselessness. `graph_evidence` is empty for a text-only match, so its
absence is itself signal.
SemanticChunk.title: SemanticChunk

SemanticRefKind.description: research-os entities a semantic doc id resolves back to.
SemanticRefKind.title: SemanticRefKind

SeriesNode.description:
Leaf: one stored series of the anchor run. Must resolve to EXACTLY one
catalog series — `dimensions: None` is only valid while (kind, key) has a
single dimension variant; an explicit map (incl. {}) pins the variant.
SeriesNode.title: SeriesNode

SeriesQueryRequest.description: Multi-run, multi-series read for the run page AND N-run comparison (D9).
SeriesQueryRequest.title: SeriesQueryRequest

SessionTranscriptOut.description: The complete normalized transcript document for one captured session.
SessionTranscriptOut.title: SessionTranscriptOut

SessionWorkOut.description: Everything one session touched, grouped by entity type.
SessionWorkOut.title: SessionWorkOut

ShiftNode.description:
Move a curve along the step axis. Positive `by` looks BACK (x[i-by]),
negative looks forward. Steps with no counterpart are NaN — shifting must
not wrap or clamp, which would compare a value against itself.
ShiftNode.title: ShiftNode

SmoothNode.description:
Smoothing INSIDE the expression (EMA(loss_a / loss_b) differs from
EMA-ing the rendered output). Reuses the store's _ema/_sma at the aligned
grid's full resolution. ema uses `factor`, sma uses `window`.
SmoothNode.title: SmoothNode

SpanUpsertResult.description: Typed replacement for the bare `{"upserted": n}` dict (D9).
SpanUpsertResult.title: SpanUpsertResult

StaleClientOut.description: One known, stale client included in the dashboard decision.
StaleClientOut.title: StaleClientOut

SummaryState.description: Derived UI state for a summary (badge).
SummaryState.title: SummaryState

TeamCreate.description:
POST /auth/teams. `slug` format/uniqueness is validated
server-side (app.teams.service) so the 400/409 carries a helpful message +
a collision suggestion; the model only bounds length.
TeamCreate.title: TeamCreate

TeamMemberOut.description: One active team membership joined to its human identity.
TeamMemberOut.title: TeamMemberOut

TeamMemberRoleUpdate.description:
Owner-controlled role change for an existing non-owner member.

Ownership transfer uses its own explicit request so a generic role change
can never accidentally replace the team's owner.
TeamMemberRoleUpdate.title: TeamMemberRoleUpdate

TeamWikiExcerpt.description:
A bounded glance at the team wiki (0098), plus how to get the rest.

Deliberately the same three-part shape as the MCP project card's `notes`
({text, truncated, read_all}) so the two feel like one product rather than
two independently invented excerpt formats. The one addition is `state`,
which the card does not need because its notes come off an already-fetched
row while this one costs a query that is allowed to fail.
TeamWikiExcerpt.title: TeamWikiExcerpt

TeamWikiState.description:
Whether `text` below IS the wiki, or a marker that it could not be read.

Spelled as a state rather than left to a null field because the two
absences mean opposite things and a caller has to be able to tell them
apart: `wiki: null` means this tenant has no document (or this is a
scoped/paged browse that never carries one), while `state="unavailable"`
means a document may well exist and THIS request could not read it. An
agent that got the first should stop asking; one that got the second should
try `GET /v1/wiki` before concluding the lab has no briefing.

Mirrors /v1/search's `state: ok|partial` (app/search/schemas.py) on purpose:
both are reads that would rather degrade with a marker than fail, and one
vocabulary for that across the surface beats two.
TeamWikiState.title: TeamWikiState

TokenCreate.description:
POST /v1/tokens (session-only mint). `scopes=None` inherits the caller's
role; e.g. `['read']` mints a read-only 'notebook' token. `expires_at=None`
means non-expiring (house precedent).
TokenCreate.title: TokenCreate

TokenCreated.description:
Mint response — carries the plaintext secret ONCE (never stored, never
shown again).
TokenCreated.title: TokenCreated

TokenOut.description: A token as listed (never carries the secret).
TokenOut.title: TokenOut

UnaryNode.description:
One operand, applied pointwise. Anything mathematically undefined at a
step (log of a negative, asin out of domain) becomes NaN there and is
dropped-and-counted at the end, never an error that kills the whole read.
UnaryNode.title: UnaryNode

WideColumn.description: One column of a wide (step-indexed) metric table: a distinct series.
WideColumn.title: WideColumn

WideSeriesResult.description:
Step x metric table (item 4): the pivot clients would otherwise do by hand,
aligned by step_index. Only STEPPED points participate; wall-clock-only series are
read via the long endpoints. Bounded to `max_rows` steps — `next_step` pages the
remainder by passing it back as `step_from`.
WideSeriesResult.title: WideSeriesResult

WikiIndexOut.description:
The wiki's front page: the agent's rendered overview plus the
machine-readable list of what it links to.
WikiIndexOut.title: WikiIndexOut

WikiPageOut.description:
The current document. Returned for a team that has never generated one too
-- see `app/wiki/service.read_page`: an empty team gets a well-formed empty
document at version 0, never a 404.
WikiPageOut.title: WikiPageOut

WikiPageRef.description: One row of `probe wiki list`. Carries no body.
WikiPageRef.title: WikiPageRef

WikiPageWrite.description:
A version-checked write to ONE page.

Same three-status contract as the single-document `WikiWrite` it
replaces, per page: equal version wins, stale gets 409 carrying the
current body, absent gets 428.
WikiPageWrite.title: WikiPageWrite

WikiRegenerateOut.description:
The 202 body for `POST /v1/wiki/regenerate`: a generation was QUEUED.

DELIBERATELY NOT A DOCUMENT. The wiki worker is asynchronous, so the document
is unchanged when this response arrives -- returning `WikiPageOut` here would
be a correct-looking shape carrying the OLD body, and every caller that
rendered it would show "regenerated" text that is the text it already had.
The fields below cannot be mistaken for the result of the generation.
WikiRegenerateOut.title: WikiRegenerateOut

WikiRevert.description: Copy a prior version FORWARD as a new one. History is never rewritten.
WikiRevert.title: WikiRevert

WikiSource.description:
Which wiki answered `GET /v1/wiki` during the migration to pages.

A string enum rather than a bool (`is_legacy`) because a third value is
already foreseeable -- the fallback disappears when the legacy table
does -- and because the field is read by humans in a JSON dump at least
as often as by code.
WikiSource.title: WikiSource

WikiVersionOut.description:
One row of the history list. Deliberately CARRIES NO BODY.

`wiki_page_versions.body` is a whole document, capped at MAX_TEAM_WIKI (20k).
A 50-row page carrying bodies would be a megabyte, and the caller that wants
one body already has a route for it -- reverting, or reading the current
document. The history list answers a different question ("what happened, and
which version do I want?"), and the fields below are exactly what it takes to
answer it.

`size_chars` is here so the list can show a revision that collapsed the
document without anyone fetching two bodies to diff them. It is the cheap
signal the arithmetic guard (locked decision 9) works from, surfaced to a
human for the same reason the guard uses it.
WikiVersionOut.title: WikiVersionOut

WikiVersionsOut.description:
A bounded page of history, newest first.

Paged by `before_version` rather than an offset because history is append-only
and grows at the head: a new revision landing between two requests shifts every
offset by one and silently re-serves a row the caller already saw. A version
number names a fixed point in an immutable sequence, so it cannot drift.
WikiVersionsOut.title: WikiVersionsOut

WindowNode.description:
A trailing-window reduction. `mean` duplicates SmoothNode's sma on
purpose: this node is where the rest of the window statistics live, and
splitting mean off from std would be a trap.

Partial windows at the start use what is available, and non-finite values
are excluded from every window they touch (the store's `_sma` convention).
WindowNode.title: WindowNode

WorkspaceKind.description:
The closed workspace kind vocabulary (mirrors the DB CHECK).

`SHARED` is RETIRED (decision 2026-07-16): app code never creates a shared
workspace anymore. It is kept here only so the API can still serialize a
legacy null-owner shared row on an existing install until it is retired by
`app.workspaces.retire_shared` and a future contract migration drops the kind.
WorkspaceKind.title: WorkspaceKind

WorkspaceOut.description: One dropdown entry: the dashboard's workspace switcher builds on this.
WorkspaceOut.title: WorkspaceOut

WorkspacePatch.description:
The one user-editable workspace field.

Slugs and ownership are stable server-managed identity. Names are display
labels, trimmed at the API boundary so whitespace-only values never reach
the database.
WorkspacePatch.title: WorkspacePatch

post.description:
DEPRECATED alongside `/v1/pairing-tokens`, and kept working for the same
reason: it is the manual fallback and every already-installed plugin uses it.

Devices paired here leave `ingest_tokens.authorization_id` NULL, which is why

List a run's artifacts, optionally filtered by kind, step range, folder, or name.

``kind`` matches the normalized (lowercased) column. Step bounds are
inclusive and compare against ``step_index``, so rows with no step are
excluded whenever either bound is set (SQL NULL comparison) — exactly what
step-scoped forensics ("sandbox state at steps 599..601") wants.

``prefix`` scopes to one folder and everything under it (S3 prefix semantics
over the derived ``path``): ``prefix=outputs`` returns ``outputs/loss.csv``
and ``outputs/plots/fig.png``, but not ``config.json``. Omit it for the whole
run. ``limit`` is opt-in and left unset by default: this endpoint has always
been unbounded, and capping it silently would truncate existing callers'
results with no way for them to notice.

``scope`` controls inheritance (default ``own`` = this run only, the historical
behavior — the run bundle/dashboard/``artifact_count`` are unaffected):
``all`` also returns the run's experiment- and project-level artifacts, ``inherited``
only those parent levels. The parent ids are derived server-side from the run row
(never client-asserted), so this stays RLS-oracle-safe. On an inherited scope each
row carries ``source_level`` and results are ordered nearest-wins (run, then
experiment, then project), so a ``name`` lookup resolves to the closest level at
row 0. ``name`` is an exact match (same canonical form as writes).

schema.title: Response List Run Coordinates V1 Runs  Run Id  Coordinates Get

get.description:
Stored edges PLUS the run -> artifact `produces` edges derived from
`artifacts.run_id`.

Why derive: nothing ever wrote a `produces` edge. `add_edge` is reachable
only by hand or via `probe edge add`, and `log_artifact()` does not call it,
so `lineage_edges` is empty for essentially every run -- which is why the
lineage view answered "no lineage" for runs that had plainly produced
output. The fact was never missing, only unexpressed: `artifacts.run_id` has
recorded it since the table existed.

Deriving at read time rather than materializing on artifact create means no
backfill for existing runs and no second copy to drift. Derived rows are
flagged `derived: true` and carry no `id` -- see LineageEdgeOut.

NOT covered here: `consumes`. A run declaring which asset version it read
has no recording surface at all today, so there is nothing to derive from.
That needs an SDK affordance before it can appear in this response, and an
empty `consumes` set is honest until it exists.

`limit` is OPT-IN and unset by default, matching
`/v1/runs/{id}/artifacts`: this route has always been unbounded, and capping
it silently would truncate results with no way for a caller to notice. That
matters more here than on most routes -- the defect being fixed is "lineage
reads as empty", and a silent cap would trade it for "lineage reads as 98%
complete", which is undetectable rather than merely wrong.

STORED EDGES SORT FIRST, ahead of derived ones, so a `limit` can only ever
shed derived rows. Ordering purely by recency would let a run's newest
artifacts evict a hand-written `consumes` or `evaluates_on` edge that no
other read route exposes -- turning a bound into silent data loss for the
one kind of edge someone deliberately recorded.

post.description:
Report that a run's process is still alive.

Liveness cannot be inferred from `status` alone: it is a plain column, so a
run whose process dies without a final PATCH stays 'running' forever. A
client calls this periodically (well inside `run_heartbeat_stale_seconds`).
The reaper uses whichever is newer: this heartbeat or substantive run/data
activity. Clients without heartbeat support therefore remain live while
they are writing data, but cannot stay 'running' forever after activity
stops.

Only a 'running' run is stamped. Beating a finished run would resurrect it
into the reaper's scan for no reason.

Lossless paginated raw-point export (item 5): every point exactly once, no
downsampling. `dimensions` selects one exact canonical series rather than
blending coordinate variants. Page by passing the returned `next_after_id`
back as `after_id`.

Server-side reduce/group over one metric's stepped points (item 7, 0059).

`by` splits per coordinate-axis value — repeat it or comma-separate for
multi-axis cells (`by=rank,split` -> one group per (rank, split) combination;
points missing an axis share ONE null bucket per axis); omitting it reduces
across everything at each step bucket. `where` is a JSON object of coord
filters (`where={"split":"train"}`), matched by type-faithful containment on
the canonical map — so `{"rank": 1.0}` matches the stored int 1 and never the
string "1". `step_bucket=k` groups every k steps ("per batch" / "every other
step" are step arithmetic on the typed range axis). `agg` is always EXPLICIT —
the server never guesses how to combine a metric. A `by` axis or `where` key
that names no known coordinate axis of the key is a 422, not a silent all-NULL
reduction or an empty result; a key logged under several kinds needs an
explicit `kind` (one cell must never average across kind namespaces).

Step x metric table for a run (item 4): DataFrame-friendly, aligned by step. The
long-format /metrics stays; this is the pivot a client would otherwise do by hand.

is simply empty.

``prefix`` scopes to one folder and everything under it (S3 prefix semantics
over the derived ``path``, 0029); ``limit`` is the opt-in sanity cap -- the
same folder-scoping its workspace-file sibling has, so both file surfaces
behave identically.

post.description:
Presign a direct upload INTO the team Shared folder (reuses the workspace-
file presign->confirm rails, anchored on shared_folder_id). The folder is
auto-provisioned on this first write.

delete.description:
Soft-delete a Shared file (idempotent-safe: absent/already-deleted/not-a-
shared-file -> 404). Tombstones the index doc in the same tx (D9). The R2
blob is left in place (deferred gc).

post.description:
Confirm a Shared-file upload (anchor-aware confirm; identical swap
semantics to a workspace file).

get.description:
Presigned GET for a Shared file (tenant-prefix verified, like the generic
artifact download). 404 unless the artifact is a live Shared-folder file.

post.description:
Reverse of share: move a Shared file back into the CALLER's personal
workspace (provisioned on first need). Symmetric re-anchor + index re-key +
name-collision handling: 409 by default, `replace=true` supersedes the prior
personal-workspace file atomically.

get.description: Flat single-GET (D9). Hidden when its run is soft-deleted.

schema.title: Response List Tokens V1 Tokens Get

delete.description:
CLI logout: the calling token revokes itself. 400 if the caller is a
session (there is no 'current token').

Revoke a token by id. Your own token: any writer. A teammate's token:
owner/admin (`admin` scope) AND a browser session (never a token).

get.description:
The team's wiki as ONE document -- now the multi-page wiki's FRONT PAGE.

Kept alive rather than retired because every shipped CLI, the MCP's
`get_entity(ref="wiki")` and the browse excerpt all call it, and what
they each do with the answer -- print it, quote it, orient an agent --
is still exactly right when the answer is the index page.

THE FALLBACK IS NOT A HEDGE. A team whose synthesis agent has not run
yet has no index page and, today, still has a legacy document with real
content in it. Serving an empty body in that window would tell every
reader the team has no wiki, which is both false and the single most
damaging thing this route can say. So an absent index falls back, and
`source` reports which model answered so no consumer has to guess.

REMOVAL CONDITION, so this shim does not become permanent by default:
the fallback goes when the legacy `experiment.wiki_pages` table does
(the old sweep is being deleted separately). At that point the `else`
branch is unreachable and should be deleted with it.

put.description:
410 GONE. The wiki is pages now; a whole-document write has no target.

410 rather than 404 because the distinction is the entire message: 404
says "no such route, check your URL", which sends a caller looking for a
typo. 410 says "this existed, it is deliberately gone, stop calling it"
-- and unlike 404 it is defined as PERMANENT, so a client that caches
the outcome caches the truth.

Not 426 Upgrade Required either: that status is about switching HTTP
protocol versions, and a client library that implements it literally
would try to renegotiate the connection.

The body is DISCARDED and the caller is told so in the first sentence.
The alternative -- writing it to the index page -- is unavailable (the
engine reserves `index` against writes because it is regenerated from
the other pages) and would be wrong even if it were not: the caller
asked to replace the team's wiki, and silently turning that into an
edit of one generated page is precisely the silent change of meaning
the migration rule forbids.

get.description:
The wiki's front page.

`body` is empty for a team whose synthesis agent has never run -- NOT a
404. "No front page yet" and "no such team" are different claims and
only one of them can be true for a caller holding a valid credential;
this is the same reasoning that keeps `GET /v1/wiki` from 404ing.
`entries` is still populated in that case, so a reader gets the list of
pages even before the agent has written prose about them.

Every page in the team's wiki, newest-updated first.

The engine excludes the reserved `index` type from this list, and that
exclusion is right rather than incidental: the index is generated FROM
this list, so including it would offer a page whose content is a
rendering of the rest of the response.

parameters.description: filter to one wiki_type
parameters.name: type

schema.description: filter to one wiki_type
schema.title: Type

get.description:
One page. 404 when there is no such page -- and here a 404 IS right,
unlike on the index: the caller named a resource, so being told the name
matches nothing is an answer they can act on.

put.description:
Replace ONE page, if it is still at the version the caller read.

THE 428 IS ENFORCED HERE AND NOT ON THE ENGINE, which accepts a write
with no precondition. That asymmetry is deliberate: the engine's route
has an older consumer (the dashboard, through the prbe-backend BFF)
that has never sent a version, and making the precondition mandatory
there would break it. Every caller of THIS route is new, so it can be
held to the contract that makes concurrent writing safe.

A stale write gets the engine's 409 passed through untouched, body and
all -- see `app/wiki/pages._mapped_engine_error`. The caller merges
against `current_body` without a second round trip.

post.description:
Copy a prior version of ONE page FORWARD as a new version.

Not version-checked, for the reason the single-document revert is not:
the version the caller names is the one they want BACK, and asserting
which version they are reverting FROM answers a question a revert does
not ask. History is never rewritten -- reverting to 3 appends 3's body
as version 6.

get.description:
One page's history, newest first, WITHOUT bodies.

No `before_version` cursor, unlike the single-document history: the
engine returns a page's whole history in one response and has no
paging parameter to forward. Inventing one here would mean slicing in
this process and reporting a `next_before_version` the engine cannot
honour -- a cursor that lies is worse than no cursor.

post.description:
Queue a wiki generation for this team NOW, ahead of the 04:00 sweep.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Locked decision 2 refreshes the wiki on one nightly sweep, and
that is the right cadence for a document nobody is watching. It is the wrong
cadence for the person who just corrected the thing the wiki was wrong about:
they have no way to see the document catch up, and "wait until tomorrow" reads
as "the feature is broken". prbe-knowledge shipped exactly this affordance
("Generate wiki now") beside its own nightly synthesis for the same reason.

202, NOT 200, AND NO DOCUMENT IN THE BODY. The wiki worker drains the queue in
its own Deployment; when this response is written the generation has not been
claimed, let alone run. `WikiRegenerateOut` carries `version` -- the version the
document is STILL at -- precisely so a caller can poll `GET /v1/wiki` for the
version passing it instead of assuming this call did the work.

`immediate=True` zeroes the debounce. The debounce exists to let an automatic
write settle before paying for a generation; a human pressing a button has
already settled, and making them wait out a window they cannot see is the same
failure as making them wait for 04:00.

THE ENQUEUE IS READ BACK, and that is not belt-and-braces. `enqueue_generation`
wraps its INSERT in a SAVEPOINT and swallows every exception BY DESIGN, so that
a generation request can never fail the domain write it normally rides along
with. This route has no domain write to protect: the enqueue is the entire
request. Left swallowed, a `kind` or `anchor_type` that `generation_refresh`'s
CHECK constraints reject would make this a button that answers 202 and does
nothing, forever, with one WARN line as the only evidence. So the pending row is
SELECTed back on the same transaction -- where the worker cannot yet see it, so
there is no claim to race -- and a missing row is a 503, exactly as the sweep
counts it a failure and exits non-zero.

Copy a prior revision FORWARD as a new revision.

Not version-checked, and it does not need to be: `revert` takes the row lock
before it reads the current version, so the forward copy is computed and
swapped under one lock and cannot lose a race. A precondition would only let a
caller assert which version they were reverting FROM, which is not what a
revert is about -- the version they name is the one they want back.

get.description:
The history, newest first, WITHOUT bodies.

Declared before `POST /wiki/revert` in this file for reading order -- you
discover a version here, then revert to it. FastAPI matches on the literal
path, so `/wiki/versions` cannot be shadowed by `/wiki`.

A team with no document returns an empty list, not a 404, for the same reason
`GET /v1/wiki` returns an empty document: "no history" and "no such team" are
different claims, and only one of them is true for a caller holding a valid
credential.

post.description:
OWNERSHIP TRANSFER: move a personal-workspace file into the team Shared
folder. In ONE tenant tx: re-anchor (workspace_id -> shared_folder_id),
enforce the shared active-name uniqueness, and RE-KEY the search index
(tombstone the old `workspace:<id>` doc + upsert the new `shared:<customer>`
doc, SAME file:<id> doc id). Provenance is preserved.

Permissions posture (deferred-permissions): ANY WRITE-scope team member may
share ANY personal-workspace file -- ownership is not checked; only WRITE
scope + a currently workspace-anchored artifact. A run/experiment/project
artifact is NOT a file and cannot be shared (422).

Name collision in the Shared folder: 409 by default (never auto-supersede);
pass `replace=true` to atomically supersede the prior shared file (the same
confirm-time swap the artifacts rails already use).

schema.title: Response List Workspaces V1 Workspaces Get

patch.description:
Rename the caller's own personal workspace.

Tenant RLS is necessary but not sufficient here: every member can see the
team's filing locations, but a person's workspace label belongs to that
person. The owner predicate makes teammate, legacy-shared, foreign, and
missing targets the same 404.

get.description:
Flat, name-ordered live COMPLETE files; names with slashes imply folders
(the existing explorer contract builds the tree client-side). Pending rows
are staged replacements/first uploads (review F14) -- hidden here so a
mid-upload replacement never shadows or duplicates the live version.

``prefix`` scopes to one folder and everything under it (S3 prefix semantics
over the derived ``path``, 0029); omit it for the whole workspace. The flat,
name-ordered contract is unchanged -- prefix narrows the rows, it does not
reshape them into a tree.

schema.title: Response List Workspace Files V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Files Get

delete.description:
Soft-delete a file only while it is anchored to ``workspace_id``.

The workspace predicate is part of the UPDATE, not a client-side precheck:
PostgreSQL rechecks it after a concurrent ownership move. A stale explorer
row therefore returns 404 instead of deleting the file from Shared (or from
another workspace). The index tombstone and audit event share the tenant tx.
